Package org.cibseven.connect.ai.agent.agentic

Class AgenticCaughtError

java.lang.Object
org.cibseven.bpm.engine.impl.bpmn.parser.ErrorEventDefinition
org.cibseven.connect.ai.agent.agentic.AgenticCaughtError
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable
public class AgenticCaughtError extends ErrorEventDefinition
An error definition on an activity a boundary event of a tool is attached to, which remembers what it was offered (CIB7-2166).

The engine hands the code of a BPMN error to the boundary event that catches it only through camunda:errorCodeVariable, a process variable the modeller has to ask for, and a boundary event without an error reference catches every code. Which one it was is asked of the definitions, though: the engine offers the error to the definitions of each scope in turn, and the first that catches it is the one whose boundary event runs next. Before it does, in the same command, the activity the event is attached to is cancelled, and its end listener (AgenticToolEndRecorder) takes the code from here: also when the boundary event itself continues asynchronously. The engine does not learn about the agent, and the code is kept only on the tool's performance, as an execution-local variable that goes with it.

Two kinds, both set by the parse listener:

  • in place of the engine's own definition of a boundary error event, with the same handler, code, precedence and variables, so it catches exactly what that one caught and the modeller's errorCodeVariable and errorMessageVariable are still written;
  • a watch on an activity that has boundary events, none of them an error event: it catches nothing, and only notes that an error thrown there found no handler. The engine ends such an activity as if it had completed, and its end must not count as the repair of an interruption one of its other events recorded.
An error nothing catches is noted by either kind, as long as nothing caught it after all.
